title: Case-cohort analysis with a weighted Cox model
summary: A hazard ratio from a random subcohort plus all cases, weighted to stand for the full cohort (Lin-Ying), with a robust variance.

sizing._why: Case-cohort sizing depends on the subcohort fraction and the event rate, and is not in the catalog.

pinned_defaults: R: cohort.size is the FULL cohort's size (4000), not the sample's.
R: method = 'LinYing'. cch's default is 'Prentice'; LinYing uses all the subcohort information with its robust variance. Here LinYing gives 0.700 and Prentice 0.676.
R: cch returns an UNNAMED coefficient vector; the code indexes it by position and asserts its length.
_python_not_applicable: No standard Python package implements case-cohort estimators with their variance. Weighting a Cox model in lifelines needs a robust variance with delayed entry, and lifelines 0.28.0's is wrong in that setting (andersen-gill-recurrent-events documents it). The entry is R only; recovery is checked by fitting 100 generated fixtures in R, and the full cohort (which a real study never has) serves as the oracle.
_unweighted: An ordinary Cox model on the case-cohort sample treats it as the cohort: here 0.431 against the weighted 0.700 (truth 0.588), with a falsely small standard error (0.080 against 0.135).
